status: PROPOSAL - research data only. This file is NOT authoritative simulation state and NOT renderer presentation data. It does not finalise a runtime schema. Canonical settlement/location identities (RFC 4122 UUIDv5, ADR-0009) are minted only by the atlas pipeline at integration time; the proposedId values here are research handles, not canonical IDs.
subject: R-16 historical settlement roster, eighth batch (batch 8) - envelope regions 12, 13, 17, 18, 19
envelopeRegions: 12 - Central Asia (Bactria, Sogdiana, Margiana, Chorasmia) (mid ~17); 13 - NW India / Maurya frontier (Indus, Gandhara) (mid ~17); 17 - Arabia (N Arabia, South-Arabian kingdoms, Gulf) (mid ~24); 18 - Kush, Meroe & Nubia (mid ~8); 19 - Caucasus, Bosporan kingdom & the Crimea (mid ~18)
batchScope: Central Asia under Seleucid rule (Bactria, Sogdiana, Margiana, Chorasmia and the Arian frontier); the Mauryan empire and its north-western frontier (Gandhara, the Indus, Arachosia, the Ganges plain); Arabia (South-Arabian kingdoms, the northern oases and the Gulf); Kush, Meroe and Nubia; and the Caucasus, the Bosporan kingdom and the Crimea. 84 records in total.
coordinateConvention: WGS84 decimal degrees, approximate representative points for the ancient site (not the modern town unless noted). Precision does not imply archaeological accuracy and is not a surveyed building location. Many sites in these regions are poorly located; coarse coordinates or null are used where honesty requires it.
idScheme: proposedId = r16-cas-<slug> (region 12), r16-ind-<slug> (region 13), r16-ara-<slug> (region 17), r16-nub-<slug> (region 18), r16-cau-<slug> (region 19); the slug (key) is region-scoped to avoid homonyms. Stable, human-readable, non-canonical.
methodNote: Records are compiled from independent evidence (primary literary/administrative sources, archaeology and the Pleiades gazetteer for coordinates). Game/mod faction names are discovery leads only and never authorities. Every coordinate is a representative point with an explicit location confidence; where only a broad location is known the coordinate is coarse or null. Political authority is recorded only where supported; otherwise it is left unclaimed.
sourceAuditNote: Pleiades gazetteer identifiers are recorded only as 'Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)', never asserted: automated access to pleiades.stoa.org was blocked by the site's anti-scraping protection during this pass, so no Pleiades id has been verified. Coordinates are approximate representative points, not surveyed locations. ALL literary sources used here post-date 278 BCE and are dated in each record: Arrian, Strabo, Pliny, Ptolemy, Quintus Curtius Rufus, Diodorus Siculus, Plutarch, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (1st c. CE), later Arabic/Persian/Georgian tradition and the medieval geographers. South-Arabian, Dedanite/Lihyanite, Minaean, Qatabanian, Hadhramite, Meroitic and Sabaic inscriptions are a partly-contemporary epigraphic corpus that also extends after 278 and is treated as evidence, not as a 278 snapshot. Earlier sources (Achaemenid administrative texts and royal inscriptions, Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian records, the Behistun inscription) are flagged as earlier. The campaign horizon is critical for dating: Central Asia is Seleucid, NOT yet Greco-Bactrian (c.250 BCE) and not Indo-Greek/Kushan; NW India is Mauryan under Bindusara, with Ashokan-era names and Buddhist foundations later; the Nabataean, Himyarite, Christian Nubian, Roman, Byzantine, Genoese and Tatar phases are all later. Confirming Pleiades ids and coordinates manually remains an integration prerequisite.
politicalContext278Bce: Central Asia (region 12) is under Seleucid control in the reign of Antiochus I Soter: Bactria, Sogdiana and Margiana are Seleucid satrapies/territories, and Antiochus I is credited (Strabo) with refounding and walling Alexandria/Antiochia in Margiana; the independent Greco-Bactrian kingdom of Diodotus (c.250 BCE) and the later Indo-Greek and Kushan periods must NOT be retrojected to 278. Chorasmia is a local eastern-Iranian polity, not securely tied to Seleucid administration. NW India (region 13) is the Maurya empire under Bindusara (r. c.298-273); Gandhara, the Indus and Arachosia came under Mauryan administration after the Seleucid-Mauryan settlement c.303 BCE; Ashokan-era names, edicts and Buddhist foundations are later than 278 and Mauryan-era names are used. Arabia (region 17) is divided among the South-Arabian kingdoms - Sabaea/Ma'rib, Ma'in/Qarnaw, Qataban/Timna, Hadhramaut/Shabwa - with Himyar still rising later; the northern oasis polities (Dedan/Lihyan, Tayma, Dumah) with the Nabataean expansion still later; and the Gulf trading cities (Gerrha, Tylos/Bahrain, and a long-faded Dilmun). Kush (region 18) is the Meroitic kingdom centred on Meroe with Napata's continuing religious centrality; the later Christian Nubian kingdoms are anachronistic. The Caucasus and Crimea (region 19) hold the Spartocid Bosporan kingdom (under Scythian/Sarmatian pressure), the independent Greek poleis of the Crimea (Chersonesos and others), Colchian Greek emporia, and the forming Iberian (Kartli) and Caucasian Albanian kingdoms; later Roman, Byzantine, Genoese and Tatar phases are anachronistic.
duplicateGuard: None of these records reproduce the 23 active atlas sites, the 12 deferred atlas candidates, the excluded site (Cosa), or any of the batch-1 (r16-ita-) or batch-2 (r16-gre-, r16-ana-) records. The prefixes r16-cas-, r16-ind-, r16-ara-, r16-nub- and r16-cau- are disjoint from all earlier batches and from each other; sites adjacent to other regions (e.g. Aria near Iran) are treated once, here.

records.existenceEvidence: Capital of the Bactrian satrapy under the Achaemenids and a major urban centre of the Iranian east, repeatedly central to Alexander's campaigns; under Seleucid rule at 278.
records.architectureContext: Walled oasis city with a citadel (Bala Hissar) and extramural settlement; mudbrick/rammed-earth construction typical of the Bactrian plain.
chronologyNotes: Achaemenid and earlier Iron Age occupation; a Seleucid provincial seat at 278.
Greco-Bactrian capital only after c.250 BCE - after the campaign.
anachronismWarnings: Do NOT show Bactra as a Greco-Bactrian or Kushan capital at 278.
Do not use the later Islamic/medieval Balkh footprint.

Behistun inscription of Darius I (earlier, 6th c. BCE, for the satrapy)

records.existenceEvidence: The Greek city at Ai Khanoum is a major Hellenistic foundation on the Oxus with a 3rd-c. BCE urban phase; the ancient name is debated and the traditional identification with Alexandria on the Oxus is not certain. On current chronology the fortified Greek city begins c.300 BCE, so a Seleucid-era settlement is probable at 278.
records.architectureContext: Walled city at the confluence of the Oxus and Kokcha with a monumental Greek civic core; the classical Greek architecture (theatre, gymnasium, temples) belongs to the developed 3rd-2nd c. phases.
chronologyNotes: Greek city phase from c.300 BCE; the great monuments belong to the 3rd-2nd c. BCE.
Destroyed c.145 BCE (later).
anachronismWarnings: Do not show the mature Greco-Bactrian monumental city of the 2nd c. BCE at 278.
Identification with Alexandria on the Oxus is NOT certain.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Whether the site is Alexandria on the Oxus or a separate foundation.
